subject: Hot-path redundancy SLA exception request
summary: FinCore requests an SLA carveout for a set of 'hot-path' endpoints that require sub-50ms tail latency and an accelerated regional failover commitment. Internal thread coordinates technical feasibility, cost/penalty adjustments, and proposes specific RTO/RPO and fallback behaviours for contract amendment.
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@fincore.com>
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Cc: platform@fincore.com
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Hot-path redundancy: request for SLA carveout (FinCore)

Hi Rohan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput and cost profile looked promising. As we scope the pilot, a follow-up ask came from our Core Payments team: a small set of endpoints (payment-risk scoring + real-time tokenization) sits on the "hot path" of their authorization flow and must meet unusually tight latency and availability requirements.

Specifically they asked whether Redwood can support an SLA carveout that guarantees:
- 99.99% availability for the hot-path endpoints (separate from standard API SLA)
- regional failover RTO <= 45 minutes for those endpoints
- RPO <= 5 minutes for transaction KV (replication/streaming)

We understand this is outside your normal multi-region default and may require reserved capacity or special routing. Can you confirm feasibility and a rough delta in monthly committed cost? Attached is a short topology and a snapshot of observed latency on our side.

If possible we'd like a written exception proposal to take to procurement next week.

Best,
Lucy
Lucy Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, FinCore
--
Attachments: hotpath_topology.pdf (diagram), hotpath-metrics-snapshot.csv (latency samples)

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@fincore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hot-path redundancy: request for SLA carveout (FinCore)

Lucy — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. I'm looping in Marissa and Kimberly to scope this from sales and legal/ops angles.

Quick notes after a first pass:
- Technically feasible with a "hot-path" reserved pool + stricter KV-cache replication; we'll need to pin model variants and a dedicated routing policy so requests never hit lower-priority pools.
- Costs: non-trivial incremental committed capacity (GPU + streaming replication); I'll get a ballpark by EOD Monday.
- Risk/penalties: we should define a bounded penalty and a rollback path (e.g., fallback to standard SLA with degraded throughput) so our risk is capped.

Kimberly — can legal/contracting start a one-page amendment template? Marissa — can you prepare an initial committed-cost estimate and the options (full reserved pool vs burstable dedicated + pre-warm)?

Next step: propose an exception term sheet we can send to Lucy that contains specific RTO/RPO numbers, failover scope, and the cost delta.

Thanks,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
--
(Attachment note: forwarding hotpath files to ops channel for deeper topology review)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hot-path redundancy: request for SLA carveout (FinCore)

Rohan/Marissa — drafted a one-page amendment outline for the exception. Key legal points to consider (quick bullets):
- Make the "hot-path" endpoints an enumerated set by API path and HubSpot route IDs; amendment voids if FinCore expands endpoints without written notice.
- Define availability measurement windows (monthly rolling) and agreed measurement tooling (Redwood tracing + FinCore client-side sampling).
- Penalty cap: propose credit equal to 25% of monthly hot-path fees for a single failure event, with annual cap at 100% of 12 months of hot-path fees.
- Failover scope: amendment only guarantees regional replica activation for listed endpoints; full cross-region warm-standby (stateful KV) requires the dedicated streaming replication option.

I've attached the brief (proposed-sla-amendment.docx) and highlighted the RTO/RPO fields. If we accept FinCore's desired RTO 45m and RPO 5m, operations will insist on either:
A) Dedicated reserved pool + continuous replication (higher cost, predictable latency), or
B) Hybrid: reserved routing + async replication + fast catch-up (lower cost but RPO cannot be guaranteed under large regional outage).

Marissa — need your cost delta and which of A/B we recommend.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
VP, Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
--
Attachment: proposed-sla-amendment.docx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hot-path redundancy: request for SLA carveout (FinCore)

Team — cost/ops summary from scoping call with infra:
- Option A (Dedicated reserved pool + continuous streaming replication): estimated incremental commit = $48k/month. Provides predictable <20ms p95 tail and supports RTO <= 30m and RPO <= 1-2m for the hot-path endpoints.
- Option B (Hybrid, reserved routing + async replication): estimated incremental commit = $18k/month. Provides <40ms p95 tail normally, can meet RTO <= 45m and RPO ~5m under normal conditions but can degrade to higher RPO during sustained regional outage.

Recommendation: propose Option B as an initial exception with a 90-day trial window and an automatic review for Option A should any SLA incidents exceed penalty thresholds twice in the trial. That reduces FinCore's immediate cost while protecting Redwood from unlimited exposure.

I've updated the proposed-sla-amendment.docx with these options and included a sample metrics dashboard link.

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: updated-proposed-sla-amendment.docx (edits), hotpath-metrics-snapshot.csv

From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai
To: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@fincore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed exception: hot-path SLA (FinCore)

Lucy — thanks for your patience. Attached is a concise exception proposal for FinCore's hot-path endpoints. High-level summary below so procurement can review quickly:

1) Scope: hot-path endpoints enumerated in Appendix A (API path + HubSpot route IDs). The amendment applies only to these routes.

2) Commitment (Option B - initial, 90-day trial):
   - Availability: 99.99% for hot-path endpoints (measured monthly, rolling window).
   - Failover RTO: <= 45 minutes for the listed endpoints (regional switchover to pre-warmed secondary routing).
   - RPO: <= 5 minutes for transaction KV under normal operating conditions; may degrade during sustained regional outage.
   - Tail latency target: p95 < 40ms for hot-path (measured at Redwood edge).

3) Ops and controls:
   - Dedicated routing policy and prefix caching applied to hot-path traffic.
   - Monitoring/tracing: Redwood and FinCore will share a read-only dashboard and agree on measurement queries.
   - Incident rollback: automatic fallback to standard routing on repeated instability; process documented in Appendix B.

4) Commercials:
   - Monthly incremental commit: $18,000 (Option B) during trial.
   - Penalty: credits as defined in the amendment (single-event credit = 25% of hot-path fees; annual cap applies).

5) Next steps requested from FinCore:
   - Confirm the enumerated endpoints (Appendix A) and approve Option B for a 90-day trial.
   - Provide procurement contact for a statement of work/PO.

If FinCore approves, we will circulate the one-page amendment and a short SOW; after signature we will enable the routing and replication with a 2-week pre-warm window.

Thanks,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: proposed-sla-amendment.docx, hotpath_topology.pdf
